scope.flow: transferFrom allowance-based token transfer and Transfer event emission in TokenWrapper
scope.environment: Ethereum ERC-20 TokenWrapper contract and off-chain consumers of Transfer events

entities.name: block explorers, wallets, indexers, tax tools, contract integrations

statements.text: A user or contract calls transferFrom to move tokens on behalf of another address using an allowance.
The from parameter (actual token holder) differs from msg.sender (the spender/initiator).
The spender invokes transferFrom(from, to, amount) on TokenWrapper.
TokenWrapper emits a Transfer event for the transferFrom call.
The Transfer event emission substitutes msg.sender (the spender) for the from parameter instead of emitting the actual token holder whose balance is debited.
For a transferFrom call, the emitted Transfer event's from field must be the token holder whose balance decreases (the from parameter), per EIP-20.

The emitted Transfer event identifies the transaction initiator (msg.sender, the spender) as the source of the tokens rather than the actual token holder, creating a permanent incorrect record in blockchain history.
Block explorers parsing the incorrect events display the operator or router contract as the originating address, so users do not see their TokenWrapper transfers in their sent transactions list.
Wallet applications populate inaccurate transaction histories and portfolio tracking because transfers are attributed to msg.sender rather than the token holder.

Off-chain indexers, analytics dashboards, and tax reporting tools store or report incorrect sender information, attributing activity to router contracts and operators and potentially failing to detect user transfers.

Smart contract integrations listening to Transfer events (treasury tracking, token-gated access, referral tracking, rewards distribution) incorrectly credit activity to operator contracts rather than users.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the caller is unauthorized; the spender is a legitimate allowance holder, so no permissionless-caller condition is claimed.

The report asserts every transferFrom call is affected (100% likelihood) but does not provide a concrete observed transaction; impacts on explorers/wallets/indexers are described as potential downstream effects.
Internal _balanceOf accounting is stated to be updated correctly, so no on-chain balance loss or theft is claimed; only event-log desynchronization is reported.
Tax-reporting incompleteness is mentioned as a possible compliance issue but is not quantified; kept within the indexer/tax impact statement.
